mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for cyclically sensitive sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which erodes real purchasing power and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 6-month averages signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by a fall in UNRATE with constant PAYEMS) above its 12-month average for three consecutive months signals a larger working-age population entering the labor market, increasing supply and suppressing wage growth, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin preservation.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls while PAYEMS is flat for 3 months AND UNRATE < 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio above its 12-month average for six consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumption momentum, which depresses demand and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio > 12-month MA for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
